name: s81pq_qb_bankp_native

pin_regs.reason: RTL already registers every data pin at the face: wr0/wr1/wq0/wq1/aq_q/i0/i1/rq0/rq1 land in one capture flop each (*_c) before any decode, mux or SRAM access, and rd is the SRAM output register driving only the port. These two stages ARE the canonical QB +2 pipeline (ot_s81_pq_qb_pipe_native, matched by ot_s81_pq_qb_align_native 2 fixed stages); wrapper pin registers would add 2 more edges per bank read and break the fixed +2 alignment with headp/headpc and align. io_flop_at_pins anchors the RTL pin flops at their faces.

structural_change: NEW master (S-ELEM-PQ/LEGACY 2026-10-16, ROOT GAP 1): ot_s81_pq_qb_bankp_native is the QB SRAM bank of the canonical PQ hierarchy (OT_PQ_QB_PIPE + OT_PQ_QB_PHYS_SPLIT, tools/s81/pq_native_hierarchy.py), x4 in both ot_s81_pq_qb_pipe_native and ot_s81_pq_qb_pinread_native (P10 headpc); it had no kit. Same 142.56x86.4 footprint and S aq_q / N rd / W control faces as the legacy bank0..3 slot (no new footprint); one 128x256 1R1W SRAM; every pin registered in RTL (capture + output register = the canonical +2). | b2: b1 gate (038cb3a78) floorplan showed rd packed into ~15 um at the N-W corner, aq_q in two corner clusters on S and clk near the SW corner -> explicit even per-face spread (spread_face_pins.py; clk at the W-face centre). Util 37% WARN kept on purpose: the outline is set by the 94.8x41.1 SRAM plus the 20 um macro channels to the two wide pin faces (N rd 256, S aq_q 512); it is the existing legacy bank0..3 die slot (drop-in, no new footprint).

job.purpose: S81 PQ QB pipelined SRAM bank (x4), canonical +2 QB pipeline
